company: Centuria Industrial REIT (Centuria Property Funds No. 2 Limited as Responsible Entity)
title: Directors' & Employees' Securities Trading Policy

tiers.name: Directors
tiers.description: A Director of the Group. Subject to the same blackout-period ban and inside-information prohibition as Employees, but the policy does not expressly require Directors to obtain prior consent before dealing outside a blackout period; Directors must instead report trades to the Company Secretary immediately so the Company or Responsible Entity can meet its ASX Listing Rule 3.19A 5-business-day notification obligation.

tiers.name: Employees
tiers.description: Any employee of the Group, including Key Management Personnel as defined in AASB 124. Must seek the consent of the Company Secretary (or the CEO in their absence) before dealing in Centuria Securities and may be required to provide copies of trading confirmations to the Company Secretary afterwards.

windows.start_anchor: the shorter of six weeks before the expected release of the Preliminary final report, or the Company's financial year-end
windows.end_anchor: the day following the actual (or expected) release to the ASX of the Preliminary final report

windows.start_anchor: the shorter of six weeks before the expected release of the Half-year report, or the end of the Company's half-year financial period
windows.end_anchor: the day following the actual (or expected) release to the ASX of the Half-year report

ad_hoc_blackout_authority: The Board may determine any other period to be a blackout period. Not confidential in the individual sense: the Company Secretary (or delegate) emails all Directors and Employees when a blackout period commences and ceases.

rules.detail: 'Centuria Securities' is defined to include only derivatives 'issued by the Group' (e.g. employee plan options), not third-party instruments written over the securities. Dealing is undefined beyond 'buy, sell or otherwise trade in Centuria Securities', so an OTC put/call written by a bank over existing shares is not expressly caught; only a resulting sale, delivery or other trade of the physical shares would be a 'dealing'.
No hedging concept, defined term, or restriction anywhere in the policy.
No mention of prepaid forwards, collars, or other monetisation structures.
Short selling is not named or restricted.
CFDs are not named or restricted.
No margin lending provision anywhere in the policy.
Granting security, a charge, lien or pledge over Centuria Securities is not addressed and is not listed as a form of dealing.
No secured financing, collateral or lending-against-securities provision anywhere in the policy.
No minimum holding period or short-term dealing restriction; only the excluded-trading carve-out for acquisitions under the Centuria Employee Deferred Share Plan or Executive Incentive Plan.

clearance.approver: Company Secretary (or the CEO in their absence)
clearance.evidence: Employees must seek the consent of the Company Secretary or in his/her absence, that of the CEO, before dealing in Centuria Securities.

clearance.post_trade_deadline: immediately after the trade (to enable ASX notification within 5 business days under Listing Rule 3.19A)
clearance.evidence: Directors must immediately report any trades in Centuria Securities to the Company Secretary once the trade has taken place by electronic means.

exceptions.approver: Chairman of the Board or CEO
exceptions.evidence: If a Director or Employee is in severe financial hardship or there are other exceptional circumstances such that the sale or disposal of the Centuria Securities is the most reasonable method available to alleviate the exceptional circumstances ... the Director or Employee ... must: write to the Company Secretary before the proposed sale or disposal.

exemption_authority: Chairman of the Board or CEO has sole discretion to judge whether exceptional circumstances (e.g. severe financial hardship) justify approving a sale or disposal during a blackout period, including on conditions; the Company Secretary communicates the outcome.

bespoke_clauses.clause: Centuria Securities: securities of any class, notes, options bonds or any related derivatives issued by the Group.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Because only Group-issued derivatives are 'Centuria Securities', an OTC put/call written by a bank over an executive's existing vested shares is not itself within the defined dealing universe, so entry into the collar is not expressly regulated.

bespoke_clauses.clause: The policy contains no reference to margin lending, other secured financing, encumbrance, hedging, short selling, stock lending or CFDs.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: A loan secured on the collared shares is not prohibited by this policy, but the complete silence also means there is no bank-facing disclosure or consent carve-out to rely on if a dispute arises; general insider-trading and blackout principles would still govern any resulting sale or transfer of the shares.

bespoke_clauses.clause: Procedures for Directors reporting on trading in Centuria Securities ... Directors must immediately report any trades ... The consent requirement in paragraph 12 is addressed only to 'Employees'.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: A Director entering or unwinding a collar outside a blackout period may not need prior Company Secretary/CEO consent at all under this policy, only post-trade notification, easing execution timing (subject to the separate blackout and inside-information bans).

bespoke_clauses.clause: Directors and Employees are not permitted to buy, sell or otherwise trade in Centuria Securities during a "blackout period".
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Entering a cash-settled OTC derivative that does not itself involve buying or selling the underlying shares may fall outside the blackout ban, though delivery, exercise or a forced sale of the physical shares would not.

bespoke_clauses.clause: the sale or disposal of the Centuria Securities is the most reasonable method available to alleviate the exceptional circumstances
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: The only blackout carve-out is framed around a sale/disposal for hardship reasons, so it would not obviously extend to establishing a collar or granting security for a loan during a blackout period.

summary: CIP's trading policy (Centuria Capital Group's Directors' & Employees' Securities Trading Policy) is a bare-bones insider-trading and blackout-period policy that never mentions derivatives, hedging, monetisation, short selling, stock lending, CFDs, margin lending, encumbrance or secured financing, so none of these is expressly prohibited or made subject to clearance. A funded OTC equity collar over vested shares, and a loan secured on those shares, therefore sit outside the policy's express dealing restrictions, which are limited to buying, selling or otherwise trading 'Centuria Securities' (a term that excludes third-party derivatives not issued by the Group). Employees must obtain Company Secretary (or CEO) consent before dealing and may need to provide trading confirmations; Directors face no equivalent pre-clearance gate but must report trades immediately for ASX Listing Rule 3.19A purposes. The overriding bans on dealing while in possession of inside information and on buying/selling during a blackout period still apply to any actual sale, delivery, or forced sale of the physical shares under the collar or loan, and the only blackout carve-out (severe hardship) is framed around a sale, not derivative entry. Overall, a funded collar appears structurally available under this policy, subject to ordinary insider-trading and blackout timing discipline rather than any specific financing or hedging prohibition.
